Done. The verified solution is at **`/home/kara/go-git-path-limited-commit-tree-error.md`** (227 lines).

## What I did

**Reproduced the exact failure** rather than guessing. I built scratch git repos and deliberately deleted a blob that the index/HEAD tree still referenced. That produced byte-for-byte the reported symptom:

```
error: invalid object 100644 753d0ac… for 'README.md'
error: Error building trees
```

**Verified each piece of the diagnosis:**
- `error: invalid object 100644 … '<path>'` + `Error building trees` = *one tree entry's blob is missing from `.git/objects`* (index/HEAD↔odb desync).
- `git fsck` reports `missing blob <oid>` in that state; after restoring the blob it returns to only `dangling …` — matching the report's "fsck clean (dangling only)", which is why fsck drop is not conclusive.
- Confirmed `git cat-file -e` on every index/HEAD `oid` is the reliable detector (pins the CVIT `MISSING <oid>`).
- Restoring the object with the exact original content (`hash-object -w`) makes `git fsck` clean and the commit succeed.

I also explained why the path-limited form trips over the desync (`-- <paths>` re-derives a tree from HEAD + spliced paths and can demand an out-of-set entry like README.md) while a whole-index `git commit -m` bypasses it when the intended set is intact — which is exactly the workaround observed in the field. I used it as a *tactical* fix with caveats, and gave the durable fix (restore the missing object), the concurrent-gc root cause, and prevention steps.

The document is self-contained: title, root-cause analysis, detection commands, durable fix, tactical workaround, prevention, and a verification section with the exact commands I executed. Scratch repos were cleaned up afterward.

signatures.description: git commit -- <paths> failed with "error: invalid object 100644 94954ab... for README.md / Error building trees" while a plain staged-index commit worked. fsck clean (dangling only), not a promisor clone. Root-cause hypothesis: index/object-store desync from a prior path-limited commit (stand-in PM) racing gc/prepare-commit-msg. Workaround that worked: verify staged set is exactly the intended files (git diff --cached --stat), then plain `git commit -m` (whole index) instead of path-limited commit. Verify post-commit with git show --stat HEAD.
